Does the answer depend on the pooling method?

With two or three studies the Cochrane Handbook (10.10.4.4–10.10.4.5) asks for a sensitivity analysis comparing interval methods rather than a choice between them. Both are given here; the published interval is the first row.

Table 8. Does the answer depend on the pooling method?
IntervalMethodSummary (95% CI)
as published0.9074 (0.831 to 0.9908)
sensitivity (Handbook 10.10.4.5)REML with Hartung-Knapp, t on k-1 = 1 degree(s) of freedom (t = 12.7062)0.9074 (0.5132 to 1.6045)

The published point is 0.9074 and the house-rule point is 0.9074. The number a reader remembers does not move; what differs is the precision claim. That is why nothing downstream catches this -- every memorable quantity survives.

A floor of 1 is applied to the variance-inflation factor so the adjustment can never narrow an interval below the unadjusted one. That guard is the recognised modification for exactly this instability, and its existence is evidence the small-k behaviour is a known problem with known handling rather than a novel judgement.

And this trial has two co primariesCV death or hospitalisation for heart failure is registered at the same rank. This review used the MACE composite and recorded no reason. Choosing between co-primaries is an analytic decision and an unrecorded one is not a methodological choice, it is an accident that happens to have a direction.
A a published synthesis carried more trials than this poolA published synthesis of this question included 3 trials where this pool carries 2. Source: Kluger et al., Reviews in Cardiovascular Medicine 2018, PMID 31032602, 'Cardiorenal Outcomes in the canvas, declare-timi 58, and empa-reg outcome Trials'.

C what this means for the estimate aboveThe estimate above is computed from the trials this object carries and is not withdrawn or altered by this note. What a reader is owed is the scope: a larger evidence base on this question exists in the literature, and whether this review's search should be widened is a decision that has not been made.
It reports the three trials side by side and does not pool.
The finding of this comparisonA published systematic review of these exact trials looked at them and did not pool them. 2018 reported the three CVOTs side by side and concluded that matching inclusion criteria and endpoints would be needed 'to ensure a truly direct comparison of the drugs'. They name the difference: Empa-reg outcome required prior confirmed cardiovascular disease and enrolled 99.2% with CVD, against 40.6% in DECLARE-TIMI 58. This object pools those two populations into one odds ratio of 0.9074. The comparison therefore does not adjudicate our estimate -- it questions whether the pool should exist. Withdrawing or restating it is a content decision and is not made here.

No bibliographic search for primary trials was run. The 2 included trials were identified by reading named registrations on the dates recorded on each entry. The basis on which this object was verified is not recorded. What this object does not claim is not recorded. The bar this object had to clear is not recorded. Results

The pooled odds ratio for the four trial-declared outcomes named in the title was 0.907 (0.831 to 0.991) across 2 trials.1

This pool is referred, not withdrawn. The stroke component is not the same component. EMPA-REG's 3-point MACE counts non-fatal stroke of any type; declare's counts ischemic stroke only. Haemorrhagic stroke is inside one composite and outside the other. Two different endpoints sharing a name. Declare registers two co-primaries and this review silently used one. The other -- CV death or hospitalisation for heart failure -- is at the same rank and is the endpoint on which declare was positive. An unrecorded selection among co-primaries is an unrecorded analytic decision. The obstacle is in the evidence. Withdrawing a published estimate is a published-number decision and belongs to Mahmood. The estimate is unchanged; the finding is complete and stated.2

Noted on this pool. A published synthesis of this question included 3 trials where this pool carries 2. Source: Kluger et al., Reviews in Cardiovascular Medicine 2018, PMID 31032602, 'Cardiorenal Outcomes in the canvas, declare-timi 58, and empa-reg outcome Trials'. The third trial is named: the canvas Program. It is in the title of the review and is not carried by this object. This is the only topic in the corpus where a trial we do not pool can be named. The estimate above is computed from the trials this object carries and is not withdrawn or altered by this note. What a reader is owed is the scope: a larger evidence base on this question exists in the literature, and whether this review's search should be widened is a decision that has not been made.3

The trials' results were closely consistent with one another: I-squared, the share of the variation between them that is more than chance alone would produce, was 2.27%; the estimated variance of the true effects between trials (tau-squared) was 0.000106, the heterogeneity test statistic Q was 1.02, on degrees of freedom 1.4

The grounds for pooling are recorded as: The extractor recovered a pooled result from this page, so the page pooled these trials. Whether they should have been pooled is not established by conversion - several pages in this corpus pooled harm with efficacy, or distinct agents, and their estimates were withdrawn for that reason. Where a later pool on this page rests on the same grounds, they are not restated.5

The full model output for every pooled outcome -- the call, the estimator, the heterogeneity statistics and the back-transformed interval -- is reproduced verbatim as Extended data at the end of this article, so every number above can be checked against the software that produced it.6

Discussion

No bibliographic search for primary trials was run. The 2 included trials were identified by reading named registrations on the dates recorded on each entry; The basis on which this object was verified is not recorded. What this object does not claim is not recorded. The bar this object had to clear is not recorded.. PubMed E-utilities esearch + esummary, executed 2026-08-20. Query as executed: (("SGLT2"[tiab] OR "sodium-glucose"[tiab] OR empagliflozin[tiab] OR dapagliflozin[tiab]) and ("cardiovascular outcome"[tiab] or MACE[tiab] OR "major adverse cardiovascular"[tiab])) and (meta-analysis[pt] OR "systematic review"[pt] OR meta-analysis[tiab]). Whether that is broad enough for the claim this review makes is the author's judgement.1

Limitations

What this review does not give a clinician: the number of events in each arm, any absolute effect or number needed to treat and how long participants were followed. A relative effect cannot be turned into the benefit or the risk facing one patient without them, so this review can support a judgement about what these trials found and not a judgement about what to do.1

Reporting guidelines

This review reports against PRISMA 2020. A screening record is held on this object and the flow it supports is shown in the Methods. The completed PRISMA checklist and FLOW diagram are not held here: the venue requires them deposited in an approved repository with a DOI cited in the Data Availability Statement, and minting that DOI is an author action rather than a build step.1
